item.title: Possible Keter Class article Hurricane Omega: Possible Keter Class article Hurricane Omega
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Other: Keter Class Scenario

Genre (Optional): Other: Apocalypse Scenario

Elevator Pitch: What if there was a Hurricane season so bad that all the named storms were used and they went to the End of the Greek Alphabet. And Hurricane Omega becomes a Keter class Hurricane.

Central Narrative: The story will follow the survivors of this storm thrashed world where the SCP try to use weather manipulating SCPs to stop it but they all fail or make the storm worse.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Not sure on this, part of what I am looking for advice on.

Additional Notes: This is just a rough idea right now. I will sit down and write out the story if there is any real interest in it. I live on the Gulf Coast so the idea of a Hurricane so powerful it could end the world is interesting to me.

item.title: Killbox & Co.: Re: Killbox & Co.
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for replying so soon!

The grotesque car deaths are the hook of the story, something to reel the reader in. It's only really just a few police reports at the beginning to make you go "Dude holy shit" or "Hey - this is Final Destination". But then the reader starts asking questions like "How?" and "Why?". So:
The meat is the car lot itself. I wanna lead the reader on, make them think the staff knows what's going on, and then have the twist that they're all terrible amnesiacs. Now the reader wants an answer. The encounter with Killbox is the climax, and with that I wanna introduce him as a second element to the story - then leave it up to the reader to figure out how to connect the dots after the read. It should also help to put Killbox in a Level 3 subsection to give him some more weight and to nicely separate the text.

item.title: The Monster that Didn't Exist: Re: The Monster that Didn't Exist
item.content:encoded:
This is a fairly decent start. You've got a heightening sense of tension, ways to speed things along without getting crazy with the timer.

1) Show at least two or three scientists getting weapons. If you really want to be fancy, show one getting to a weapons locker before getting killed, one getting a weapon before being killed, and the third shooting but missing before he's killed.

2) The scream in his ear should increase in volume with each death. It should help your tension just a little more and add to the end.

3) Also, you need to have the "There can be only ten" come out somehow at least three ways before he gets it. Yeahyeah, I know I'm giving you lots of patterns to play with and I'm probably going over somehow. However, that's because patterns have strength, and I figure that hearing it just once just makes it a random message.Backing with a pattern makes it hard to ignore.

But great start!

Otherwise, great start!

item.title: Harrowing Haberdashery: Re: Harrowing Haberdashery
item.content:encoded:
1) I'm sort of split on the propagation. First, it defeats the purpose of not being overpowered when it can basically duplicate itself hundreds of time, and it also makes it hard for The Foundation to find all of those needles. On the other hand, it makes it into a potential plague and that's sort of an interesting concept.

All I can suggest here is that you may want to put a duration on the longevity of the duplicated needles of maybe a week.

2) Also, just to make things interesting from a dramatic perspective, a duration on how long the effect can last would be interesting as well (there's just something I like about a woman giving her staff the whatfor and then realizing she screwed up); otherwise it just feels like you're creating SCPs that will have a long duration, and are likely to be destroyed or at least retired once someone makes the connection.

3) I think people are bored with SCPs that only do negative things in a negative way. It would be interesting if it magnified ANY emotion that the seamstress had while using it. Also, point out that people prick their thumbs a lot while sewing, especially while emotionally distracted; that's they invented thimbles!

The combo of expanding its ability and pointing out how often it happens ups it threat level a little, and in potentially interesting ways.

Otherwise, a good start!

item.title: A Deconstruction of the Foundations Modus Operandi (SCP): Re: A Deconstruction of the Foundations Modus Operandi (SCP)
item.content:encoded:
This does feel too much like a zombie plague to me… yeah they're not undead but otherwise its similar

We discover that SCP-1609 (and many others) are completely fabricated. They don't exist. They are nothing but Foundation propaganda, a way to convince Foundation personnel that the GOC are incompetent and the Foundations way is the correct way… the only way, to deal with the anomalous. Moreover, they serve as a warning to those who would try to preemptively neutralise an anomalous object.

I feel like a new SCP author's article should depend on other articles quite this much without seeming like you are trying to gain credibility by latching onto those other articles… also, not a big fan of this concept, as all of these things were classified so its not like they're cover stories… only those cleared for each would know of them. Its like a cover from a very small niche group of people…

Also, as a Jewish man, I am uncomfortable with this stuff:

Due to the anti-Semitic slur scorched into the corpse's chest, Foundation historians have theorised that the corpse was murdered due to the Christian persecution of the Jewish populace admist the onset of the Bubonic Plague.

&

it is implied the phenomenon manifested due to the lynching of the poor Jewish gentlemen, who was repeatedly burned as a form of torture. The reason why the infection can only be destroyed through incineration is because those that killed Parisian Man used fire to burn him, even though he wasn't infected.

Are you Jewish? Because honestly this level of grindhouse torture porn stuff based on anti-semitic violence for the sake of entertainment is… just a bad look personally.

item.title: A box that a person can step through to another world: JS Staff Post -- Forum Crit -- Info
item.content:encoded:
Author,

Per the required reading forum guidelines, please fill out the concept template to seek feedback on your idea:

 **Seeking Greenlights:** Put yes or no. **Page Type:** SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) **Genre (Optional):** Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify) **Page Layout (Optional):** [How will you will structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? If you plan on using a unique format/format screw, describe that here.] **Elevator Pitch:** [What is the basic core idea? Use a bullet point list if necessary.] **Central Narrative:** [Describe the story beats or overarching context/"big picture" for your piece. If there is no story content, put "none".] **Hook/Attention-Grabber:** [What is novel/unique about your premise? What is special about your idea here that will make it stand out among the other works already on the mainsite?] **Additional Notes:** [Note any concerns or particular areas of assistance you would like reviewers to focus on.]

Rather than posting a new comment, edit your previous post using the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your first comment.

Remember that the combined text for your answers to the last four sections (Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention-Grabber, and Additional Notes) MAY NOT exceed 400 words. For convenience, authors can use this page to check wordcount: https://wordcounter.net/

Once you have revised your post accordingly, please reach out to reviewers to request that they look at your thread. You can find example lists of contacts in the Required Reading thread linked above.

item.title: The Mother of Meteorites: The Mother of Meteorites
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • Extraterrestrial animals that fly through space with telekinesis, feeding on planetary ring systems and other space debris and adding the matter to their rocky shells.
  • Look like rocks with organs inside, like Pyura chilensis. Could even use that animal for the picture, possibly.
  • Possibly silicon-based and composed entirely of biological rocks, if that's semi-plausible.
  • Reproduce through parthenogenesis, since they rarely cross paths in space. When ready to reproduce, they fall back to the planet of their birth, burning up in the atmosphere but leaving behind several metallic eggs in the crater.
  • After hatching, the babies consume some of the rocks in the area to build their shells before returning to space.

Central Narrative: The Containment Procedures involve traveling to locations of meteorite impacts to ensure that no civilians find any eggs, monitoring of asteroids to identify possible instances and predict their impact times and locations, and preventing NASA from detecting them. The description provides information on their biology and behavior. There's an addendum at the end chronicling observations of some captive instances and an experiment to see how they do in a non-space environment with gravity. No big twist.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is one of those strange, but not really dangerous, anomalies that does a good job of conveying the weirdness and wonder of the SCPverse without being horrific or grimdark. It's also kind of cute, I guess.

Additional Notes: Do I need to make them more dangerous? If so, I can just make it so the mother survives the impact and grows larger each time, meaning that her periodic returns to the same planet cause increasingly worse disasters at regular intervals. Then the procedures would involve destroying any recovered eggs, and possibly destroying any particularly large instances likely to return to Earth in the near future. I'd really rather leave them as quirky, strange, and kinda cute things that aren't especially dangerous or horrifying, though.

item.title: The Abyss is Safe (seeking Crits and Greenlight): Re: The Abyss is Safe (seeking Crits and Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

Not so much an ethical dilemma as much as a failing on there part for just kind of not caring about the researchers there.

I mean this is an ethical dilemma… but I was referring to the decision to bury the body at sea, because you phrased it as "Of course, as cruel as the Foundation can be, they haven't killed someone and tossed the body into an ocean that preserves life, which ends up happening when the body left out on the rocky sea floor is pulled into the entrance."

The reason they are so isolated is due to the difficulty of the reaching the SCP’s Getting there would require mounting an expedition in a submersible every time, thus the teams work in monthly shifts, similar to the ISS.

This is based on the facts as laid out in the premise… but you could change that. And I suggest you do?

My suggestion is to make a more interesting conflict, and one without so many inconvenient layers to them.

If you want to focus on deep sea, I would suggest creating an anomaly that has something to do with the ocean. As it is, this doesn't seem so related (creating functional immortality, which we have way too much of personally)

If you want the narrative to be interesting, I think you need the theme and the details to be in tonal consistency with your anomaly.
